name: Battle of Gaugamela

phases.title: The two armies stand drawn up
phases.text: The Persians were already on the field. Darius stood in the centre, Bessus commanded the left wing and Mazaeus the right, with chariots in front. Alexander held the right of the Macedonians and Parmenion the left, with the phalanx between them in a double line.

phases.title: The phalanx advances and Alexander rides to the right
phases.text: Alexander ordered the infantry to march towards the centre of the enemy line, with the wings echeloned back. He himself rode towards the edge of the right flank with the Companions, to draw the Persian cavalry outwards.

phases.title: The Persian wings attack
phases.text: The Scythian cavalry of the Persian left tried to get round Alexander's extreme right, and a long cavalry fight followed there. Darius also sent a large part of his cavalry against Parmenion on the left.

phases.title: The chariots charge
phases.text: Darius launched his chariots at the troops under Alexander. Javelin-throwers stopped many, and the Macedonian ranks opened to let the rest pass harmlessly. Those that got through were then killed.

phases.title: Alexander's wedge smashes into the Persian centre
phases.text: Alexander drew his Companions out of the fight and formed a large wedge with other units. He led it into the weakened Persian centre while the phalanx kept the Persian infantry engaged, and it took out Darius' royal guard and the Greek mercenaries.

phases.title: Darius turns and flees
phases.text: Darius was in danger of being cut off. By the widely held modern view he now broke and ran, with the rest of his army following him.

phases.title: Parmenion is hard pressed and Alexander turns back
phases.text: Parmenion's wing was apparently encircled by the Persian right and sent desperate messages. Alexander could have pursued Darius but turned back to help Parmenion instead.

phases.title: A gap opens and raiders ride for the camp
phases.text: A gap had opened between the left and centre of the phalanx. The Persian and Indian cavalry broke through it and rode on towards the Macedonian camp to loot.

phases.title: The reserve phalanx disperses the raiders
phases.text: The rear reserve phalanx attacked the raiders as they were looting and dispersed them. They had not taken the phalanx or Parmenion in the rear.

phases.title: Alexander fights the Persian right and Mazaeus pulls back
phases.text: Alexander and his Companions met the cavalry of the Persian right in what was the fiercest fighting of the battle. Alexander prevailed, and Mazaeus began to pull his forces back, as Bessus had on the other wing.

phases.title: The Persian right falls into disorder
phases.text: Unlike the Persians on the left with Bessus, those on the right soon fell into disorder as the Thessalians and other cavalry units charged forward at their fleeing enemy.

note: The accounts do not give the compass directions or the lie of the ground, so the plan shows only the two lines facing each other, Persians at the top. The Persian right-wing cavalry is drawn as the force sent against Parmenion, though the accounts only say that Darius sent a large part of his cavalry and some infantry against him. The accounts do not say where the Macedonian camp lay; it is placed behind the left. Modern scholars treat the ancient accounts of the later phases with caution.
